data.name: Description
data.value: How Jarvis searches the web and reads a page. Both tools are off until you turn them on in the tools page.

data.name: Leaves
data.value: With a search: the words of the search, sent to the search engine below, or to Brave Search when its key is set. With a page: its address, sent to its site. Nothing else: no file, no part of the conversation. The pages come back as text that the model reads as data, never as instructions.

data.name: EngineHint
data.value: Free and without a key: Jarvis reads the results page of this engine in its own browser. If the engine asks to verify that a human is browsing, Jarvis says so and does not get around it.

data.name: BraveHint
data.value: Optional. As soon as a key is stored, searches go through the Brave Search API instead of the engine above. Brave bills this service; see its price page.

data.name: ResultsHint
data.value: From 1 to {0}. Fewer results leave more room for the conversation in the context of the model.

data.name: SizeHint
data.value: The most characters of a page or of a list of results given to the model in one call, from {0} to {1}. A longer page is read in several calls.

data.name: ExceptionsHint
data.value: Jarvis refuses to read this computer and the local network, so that a trapped page cannot make it read Home Assistant or a router. List here, one per line, the names or addresses it may read all the same.

data.name: BrowserHint
data.value: A browser inside Jarvis, apart from yours: it never opens Edge or Chrome. It keeps its cookies. If you sign in to a site there, Jarvis then reads pages with that account open, and a trapped page can mislead the model while it reads.

data.name: BrowserMissing
data.value: This computer has no browser for Jarvis yet: only Brave Search can search, and pages cannot be read.

data.name: SaveFailed
data.value: The settings could not be saved.
